entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Licinius Cornelius Valerianus, also known as Valerian II, was the eldest son of Roman Emperor Gallienus and Augusta Cornelia Salonina who was of Greek origin and grandson of the Emperor Valerian who was of a noble and traditional senatorial family.

Valerian II ruled alongside his father from 253 CE until Gallienus' death in 261 CE, marking the beginning of the Crisis of the Third Century.

The Roman Empire's economy and military were severely weakened during this period, and Valerian II's reign is often seen as a symbol of this decline.

Despite this, Valerian II played a significant role in the empire's politics, and his death in 257 CE led to a power struggle between various claimants to the throne.

The legacy of Valerian II is complex, as his reign was marked by both significant challenges and notable achievements.

'When the power of the emperor fails, it is the duty of the gods to restore order.' - Valerian II
